artists.biography: Saint Etienne are an English electronic music band from London, formed in 1990. The band consists of Sarah Cracknell, Bob Stanley and Pete Wiggs. They are named after the French football team AS Saint-Étienne.

perplexity.description:
Words and Music by Saint Etienne, released in 2012 on Heavenly Recordings, is the eighth studio album by the English alternative dance trio Saint Etienne. The album is a celebration of music’s emotional and cultural impact, blending electronic and pop elements with lush orchestration, nostalgic melodies, and reflective lyrics. Drawing on their signature sound of shimmering synths, atmospheric strings, and smooth vocals, the band explores themes of memory, fandom, and the transformative power of songs. Collaborations with longtime associate Ian Catt, Richard X, and former Xenomania members Tim Powell and Nick Coler add depth and variety to the album’s sonic palette.

Musically, Words and Music by Saint Etienne stands as a mature and cohesive entry in the band’s discography, marking their first studio album in seven years since Tales From Turnpike House (2005). The record balances upbeat, dance-oriented tracks like “Tonight” and “DJ” with introspective moments such as “When I Was Seventeen” and “Haunted Jukebox,” showcasing the group’s ability to merge pop accessibility with emotional resonance. Upon its release, the album was praised for its thoughtful songwriting and elegant production, earning positive reviews from critics who noted its warmth and intelligence. While it did not achieve major commercial chart success, it was well-received by fans and critics alike, reaffirming Saint Etienne’s status as influential figures in the UK’s electronic and pop landscape.
